the role of GTPase activity in dynamin-mediated actin ring formation.
the role of the cytoskeleton of the osteoclast in bone resorption.
the effects of dynamin inhibition by dynasore on the bone-resorption activity of and act in ring formation in mouse ostecolasts.

the GTP-binding and GTP-hydrolysis activity of dynamin are critical for the bone resorption of osteoclast.
inhibition of the GTP binding and/or GTPase activity by dynasore disrupts the actin ring in osteoclast, which leads to the suppression of the bone resorption.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dynasore, a GTPase inhibitor of dynamin, inhibits osteoclast bone resorption by disrupting actin ring formation.
dynamin is required for the organization and maintenance of the actin rings of mature osteoclasts, and the disruption of actin rings by dynasore is sufficient to suppress bone resorption.
dynamin is a key molecule for the formation of actin ring in osteoclast.

inhibition of dynamin GTPase activity with dynasore is an effective strategy for inhibiting bone resorption.
dynasore can be used to develop a novel anti-resorptive agent for the treatment of osteoporosis.
